10.1002_adfm.202600066: Interfacial design remains a central challenge in enabling anode‐less sodium (Na) metal batteries, where stability, uniform plating, and SEI integrity must all emerge from a bare current collector. Here, we report a rational strategy to pre‐program the interphase through laser‐mediated translation of a crystalline covalent organic framework (COF) into a chemically, morphologically, and electronically optimized carbon scaffold. By selecting a porphyrin‐triazine‐based COF with extended conjugation, heteroatom functionality, and in‐plane order, we achieve a transformed C@COF surface that retains topological coherence and delivers spatially uniform sodiophilicity. Operando imaging coupled with voltammetry reveals stochastic and gas‐evolving growth on bare Cu, in contrast to smooth, synchronous Na deposition with minimal parasitic reactions on the C@COF interface. COMSOL simulations further capture how compositional and topological tuning redistributes electric field lines, flattens potential gradients, and minimizes nucleation overpotentials. This results in a high average Coulombic efficiency (∼99.4%) with exceptional stability of over 5000 cycles of reversible Na plating‐stripping and robust rate capability up to 10 mA cm −2 , ultimately achieving long‐cycling anode‐less C@COF||NVP full cells. By translating molecular architecture into interfacial function, this strategy offers a blueprint for designing kinetically intelligent and chemically adaptive interfaces, opening new directions for programmed surface engineering in metal‐anode battery systems.
10.1002_adma.202501230: Ruthenium (Ru) is considered as a promising catalyst for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet its weak water adsorption ability hinders the water splitting efficiency. Herein, a concept of introducing the oxygenophilic MgO x and MoO y species onto amorphous Ru metallene is demonstrated through a simple one‐pot salt‐templating method for the synergic promotion of water adsorption and splitting to greatly enhance the alkaline HER electrocatalysis. The atomically thin MgO x and MoO y species on Ru metallene (MgO x /MoO y ‐Ru) show a 15.3‐fold increase in mass activity for HER at the potential of 100 mV than that of Ru metallene and an ultralow overpotential of 8.5 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm −2 . It is further demonstrated that the MgO x /MoO y ‐Ru‐based anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer can achieve a high current density of 100 mA cm −2 at a remarkably low cell voltage of 1.55 V, and exhibit excellent durability of over 60 h at a current density of 500 mA cm −2 . In situ spectroscopy and theoretical simulations reveal that the co‐introduction of MgO x and MoO y enhances interfacial water adsorption and splitting by promoting adsorption on oxidized Mg sites and lowering the dissociation energy barrier on oxidized Mo sites.
10.1002_aenm.71779: Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy‐dense cathode such as Ni‐rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni‐rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co‐solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm − 2 ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah − 1 ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm − 2 ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah‐level anode‐free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.
10.1002_anie.202425277: As the “blood” of Li−O 2 batteries (LOBs), electrolytes with various solvation structures of Li + can greatly influence the composition of solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on anode and the growth kinetics of Li 2 O 2 on cathode, and further the battery performance. However, achieving delicate modulation of the multi‐composition electrolytes remains significantly challenging to simultaneously give consideration to both the anode and cathode reactions. In this work, we employed Bayesian optimization to develop advanced electrolytes for LOBs, enabling the formation of a stable inorganic‐rich SEI, and modulation of Li 2 O 2 morphologies. Thus obtained LOBs using the optimized dual‐solvent electrolyte could deliver a discharge capacity of 14,063 mAh g −1 at a current density of 500 mA g −1 , which is far higher than those using the single‐solvent electrolytes. This study not only highlights the critical role of the solvation structure for improving the battery performance, but also provides new insights and important theoretical guidance for delicate modulation of electrolyte compositions.
10.1016_j.jhazmat.2026.142177: Biodegradable mulching films have been developed as an alternative to conventional agricultural plastics; however, concerns persist regarding the microplastics (MPs) generated during their degradation. This study investigates the mobility and fate of polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT) fragments derived from biodegradable mulching films in surface runoff and infiltration under two scenarios: bare and cultivated soil. Six experimental units with soil amended with PBAT fragments (0.5 wt% in the upper 4 cm of soil) were used. Barley (Hordeum vulgare) was cultivated in three of the units. Irrigation and simulated rainfalls were applied, and natural rainfall was monitored. Runoff and infiltration water were collected over a 5-month period, and soil samples were analysed after harvesting. Results show that most biodegradable MPs remained in the topsoil. Cultivation enhanced MP retention, with 70% of particles found in the 0-5 cm layer and 29% in the 5-10 cm layer, compared with 50% and 7%, respectively, for bare soils. This suggests that vegetation reduces MP losses via runoff while promoting their movement towards deeper soil layers. Indeed, MP mobilization by runoff was very low in bare soils (1.6%), and cultivation further limited surface transport (0.02%). Less than 0.001% of MPs infiltrated through the unsaturated zone. The type of water-input event strongly influenced MP mobilization: high-intensity rainfall increased runoff-driven transport in bare soils, while the volume of infiltrating water conditions increased the penetration of MPs to deeper soil layers. Overall, this study provides critical insights into the behavior of biodegradable plastics in soil ecosystems.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c07110: Electrochemical lignin valorization provides a sustainable route to aromatics, yet its viability is limited by high overpotentials, electrode fouling, and indiscriminate bond cleavage. Herein, we present a low-cost electrocatalytic cycle, based on soluble iron complex mediators, that decouples electron transfer at the electrified interface from chemical oxidation to drive the sustained, targeted cleavage of recalcitrant β-O-4 linkages. Using a representative lignin model compound, 1-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)–2-(2-methoxyphenoxy)–1,3-propanediol, we contrast the low-spin [Fe(CN)6]3–/4– with the high-spin of the Fe(acac)3 system, demonstrating that the mediator's spin state, electrode material, and applied potential dictate reaction yield and product distribution. This enables tunable selectivity without requiring costly or synthetically demanding ligands. Mechanistic and computational studies reveal the distinct effects of outer-sphere vs inner-sphere processes of the two systems. Translating this methodology to technical lignosulfonate validates its robustness for macromolecular processing, leading to the formation of both aliphatic products (e.g., acetic acid, butanoic acid, and glycolic acid) and high-value aromatic products (e.g., o-cresol, 3,4-dihydroxy-5-methoxybenzaldehyde, and 2-hydroxyterephthalic acid).
10.1109_tie.2026.3675133: Owing to its reduced switching and inductor losses compared to traditional two-level converters, asymmetric three-level buck–boost (3LBB) converter shows its potential in universal serial bus (USB) power delivery (PD) charger application. To fully leverage its advantages across wide input and output voltage ranges, this work provides a detailed analysis of 3LBB operation modes. A novel operation mode is identified, accompanied by a corresponding modulation strategy. The proposed strategy ensures both optimized efficiency and seamless transitions between different modes. Additionally, to address the challenge of flying capacitor voltage balancing in multilevel converters, a novel balancing technique incorporating both duty cycle and phase-shift compensation is proposed. This method provides active balancing across all operating conditions and significantly enhances voltage regulation on flying capacitor under light loads compared to existing approaches. Collectively, the proposed control strategies yield substantial efficiency improvements. A 240 W prototype complying with USB PD 3.1 standards was experimentally validated. The prototype verifies the effectiveness of the proposed operation modes and voltage balancing method. An efficiency improvement of 3.2% under full load is achieved compared to two-level converter.
